04The limits

What a scan can read. What it cannot.

A recording holds what was on the screen. The report stops where the screen stops.

Can read

  • a printed ad label
  • an account name
  • a post's position in the feed
  • the date recorded
  • how many posts appeared
  • an account that returns
  • a suggested label
  • a following label
  • a headline on screen

Cannot read

  • why a post appeared
  • your beliefs
  • your mood
  • the platform's model
  • what you scrolled past
  • which tap led where
  • the whole feed
  • the next feed
  • who else saw it

We show what appeared in a sample and keep observed labels apart from inferences. Political content describes a post, not your beliefs. Tone describes a reading of the content, not your mood. A suggested post does not tell us which action led to the recommendation.

The example on this page is fictional, not a live scan or a demonstration of a running classifier. The one real scan is marked as such. This page does not record your screen or analyze your feed.

06Privacy

Your data stays yours.

A scan handles sensitive material. Here is how it is treated.

Read the privacy policy

Read, then deleted

Frames of your screen are analyzed to build the report, then deleted from your device.

Delete anytime

Deleting your account removes your scan results and profile.

Never sold

No ad tech and no analytics on this site, and your data is not for sale.

Public methodology

Each metric is documented, and the analysis prompts are published in full.

What people do with it

A read on a feed you can act on.

See which accounts fill your feed, not the ones you think do.

Which posts carried an ad label, and how many, in each scan.

Re-tune on purpose

Teach and research

Example records for classrooms studying recommender systems.
